scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Queer Tango traces back to early 20th-century Buenos Aires where men danced tango with men due to a shortage of women, especially in immigrant and brothel contexts.
This practice was suppressed as tango gained popularity in Europe and was re-imported as a heterosexual couple dance with fixed gender roles.
The modern Queer Tango movement began in 2001 in Hamburg with the first gay-lesbian milonga and the International Queer Tango Argentina Festival, reviving same-sex and open role dancing globally.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Queer Tango is danced socially at milongas and festivals that celebrate gender diversity and inclusivity.
It provides a safe space for LGBTQIA+ dancers and others to explore tango free from heteronormative constraints.
The dance challenges traditional gender norms and promotes reflection on gender identity and expression.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Queer Tango uses traditional Argentine tango music, typically featuring bandoneón, violin, piano, double bass, and sometimes vocals.
The music is in a 2/4 or 4/4 meter with a moderate tempo, characterized by dramatic, melancholic melodies and rhythmic patterns that support improvisation.
Listen for the bandoneón, violin, piano, double bass.
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4.
The music features the characteristic bandoneón-led melodies with rhythmic pulses and melancholic tones typical of Argentine tango, providing a rich emotional backdrop for improvisational dance.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes in Queer Tango vary widely, reflecting the inclusive and non-traditional nature of the dance.
Unlike traditional tango, which often features gendered attire, Queer Tango dancers wear clothing that suits their chosen roles or personal expression.
Settings include milongas, queer tango festivals, and social dance events worldwide, often organized by LGBTQIA+ communities or allies.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Augusto Balizano opened La Marshall, the first queer milonga in Buenos Aires in 2002.
Mariana Docampo started the weekly milonga Tango Queer in San Telmo in 2005.
Queer Tango scenes and festivals have developed internationally, including in Argentina, Germany, Denmark, Sweden, France, the United States, Uruguay, and Mexico.
Queer Tango descends from early same-sex tango dancing in Buenos Aires and the traditional Argentine tango couple dance.
